# The provenance file on Kalki

*Provenance record 270 · Kalki · one temple, fully accounted for.*

## Provenance

**1. The attestation.** **कल्कि** — "The avatāra yet to come — the tenth and final avatāra of Viṣṇu, who appears at the end of the Kali Yuga riding a white horse to destroy unrighteousness and restore the age of truth". On record: Mahābhārata 3.191 (the earliest Kalki prophecy), Kalki Purāṇa (the full biography), Bhaviṣya Purāṇa (the Kali Yuga lists), Kalacakra tradition (Śambhala).

**2. The narrative record.** **The Prophecy of the Horse** — The earliest Kalki-passage names the signs: when time decays, a being of immense power will be born to a family of Brahmins, swift as thought, his hand a sword, his steed white as milk, blazing like a comet.  The passage is embedded in the epic’s cosmological books as Vishnu’s promise to the tormented earth. **The Full Biography** — The eponymous Purāṇa tells it whole: the child Kalki, mocked by the corrupt, learns the Vedas from Paraśurāma himself, marries the princess Padmāvatī by the sword-contest, and rides out against the mleccha kings.  His campaigns purify the world; the wicked fall to his blade and the earth’s burden lifts at last.

**3. The physical record.** No ancient Kalki temples — he has not yet been born. But his images ride through South Indian temple friezes of the Dashavatāra, and the Śambhala iconography of Tibetan thangkas gives his myth a monumental afterlife in paint across the Himalayas.

**4. The current holding.** The temple at [/kalki/](/kalki/), a temple of the restored name. aSCII-equivalent form

**5. The documented resonances.** **Disaster Resilience & Recovery**, **Gaming, Fantasy & Entertainment IP**, **Astrology, Tarot & Esoteric Services** — seats argued and weighted in the [pattern atlas](/patterns/), read through the myths in this temple's [Resonance File](/kalki/blog/resonance/).

**6. The primary sources.** [Rig Veda](/texts/rig-veda/), [Ramayana](/texts/ramayana/) — the library this file answers to, open at the [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/).

**7. The continuing record.** Kalki is eschatology’s most durable prophetic figure in the living world: films, novels, and comics re-stage his coming endlessly, and ‘waiting for Kalki’ is an idiom for expecting the end of a corrupt order.  The Śambhala legend seeded Theosophy’s Shambhala and, through it, a century of Western occult geography.

- **Restored name:** Kalki
- **ASCII form:** kalki
- **Meaning:** "The avatāra yet to come — the tenth and final avatāra of Viṣṇu, who appears at the end of the Kali Yuga riding a white horse to destroy unrighteousness and restore the age of truth"
- **Domain of influence:** Prophecy, Renewal, Avatar of Vishnu
- **Pantheon:** Sanskrit
- **Restoration:** ASCII-equivalent form
- **Original script:** कल्कि
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 270 of 597
